title: Pages by the same scribe share more words than pages by different scribes, pages kept whole: a candidate fact the drifting chain does not copy
statement: Follows P-G-007 and P-G-008, public practice split only; nothing here is scored on hidden pages. P-G-008 showed that the section cannot be isolated on a sample of 34 pages: sections are runs of neighbouring pages, so any text that changes along the book beats a null that deals section labels among whole pages, and the rotation null has no power. I confirm that for the section (page-pair similarity, same section minus different section: 0.053 on the evaluation pages but 0.011 and 0.005 on two samples of training pages). The scribe is different, because the scribes do not sit in runs: in the herbal quires Davis's hands 1, 2 and 5 alternate by sheet, so pages far apart can share a scribe while neighbours do not. Statistic: cosine of raw word counts for every pair of pages with at least 40 certain paragraph words; median over pairs written by the same hand minus median over pairs written by different hands (hand labels from Davis 2020 as carried in the transliteration header, a palaeographic label, not derived from the vocabulary; it does largely coincide with Currier's languages, which were derived from the text). Null: the hand labels dealt at random among the pages, every page whole (199 deals). Manuscript: 0.106 on the 34 evaluation pages (Takahashi 0.099, RF 0.086), 0.118 on all training pages, 0.061 to 0.175 on six samples of 31 to 38 training pages; p = 0.005 in all nine cases. Under rotation of the labels along the page order (every offset) the manuscript reaches the floor of that test (p = 1/n, 0.029 at 34 pages) on the evaluation pages and on five of the six samples, 0.0625 on the sixth, so rotation is reported here but should not be a pass condition at this size. Generators, laid onto the evaluation pages as the scorer does: the drifting line chain behind R-012 to R-018 (window of 20 public pages) gives -0.002 to 0.075 on six runs, deal-null p 0.015 to 0.51, none at or below 0.01; with narrower windows of 10, 6 and 4 pages, two seeds each, 0.040 to -0.007, p 0.045 to 0.67 (these six texts still meet every established fact on the practice split); drift-free self-citation, contiguous or sampled, is negative (-0.04, -0.08); the plain line chain of R-011 gives -0.07. So 0 of 15 generated texts reproduce it, and narrowing the window, the obvious way to copy more of the book's local detail, does not help. Why it may be hard to copy fairly: an attacker's lines are laid onto hidden pages whose scribe the attacker cannot know; a table fitted by position averages over the scribes that alternate there. Why it may still fall: a procedure with two or more tables that it alternates by sheet, as scribes sharing a quire would, could match it if its alternation happened to line up with the hidden pages, and the present attack format gives it no way to line up; that is a limit of the format, not evidence about the manuscript, and it should be stated with the fact. Not evidence of language: scribes with different habits or different copying tables give the same picture. A reviewed code change is on branch code-L2-page-group-similarity-fleet-fable (statistic page_group_similarity by section, language or hand; nulls shuffle_page_labels and rotate_page_labels; one test). Proposed: once it is merged, register the fact by hand against shuffle_page_labels at p 0.01 (no level, no rotation condition), then send the drifting chain unchanged against it and record the outcome either way.
check: fact.json {"select": {"unit": ["P"], "certain": true}, "statistic": {"page_group_similarity": {"by": "hand"}}, "compare": [{"null": "shuffle_page_labels", "perms": 199, "p": 0.01}]} after the code change is merged; then attack.json (fact) with the R-017 text.
